title: Fewest Coins
statement:
Find the smallest number of coins that add up to an amount.

Contract
- `coins` holds positive coin values, may contain duplicates, and may be empty. Each value can be
  used any number of times.
- `amount` is zero or greater.
- Return the minimum number of coins whose values sum to exactly `amount`, or `-1` when no
  combination of the coins can make it. An amount of 0 needs 0 coins.
- Do not mutate `coins`.

Examples
- `minCoins(new int[]{1, 3, 4}, 6)` returns `2` (3 + 3).
- `minCoins(new int[]{5, 10}, 3)` returns `-1`.
- `minCoins(new int[]{7}, 0)` returns `0`.
hints: Always taking the largest coin that fits can fail. Look for a small set of coins where it does.
Let best[a] be the fewest coins that make amount a. Each best[a] extends some best[a - coin] by one coin.

Fill best from 0 up to the amount, using an unreachable marker that cannot overflow when you add one. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space with a fixed set of coin values, where n is the amount (in general O(n * number of coins)).
inputSyntax: Input: the coin values followed by the amount, for example: [1, 3, 4] 6
